title: I built a tool for my own AI gamedev workflow – now I'm releasing it for free
author: Phllori
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I originally didn't plan to release this at all.

I built **PhlloriLab** for myself, because my own game development workflow was getting increasingly messy.

  


I'm a machinist in my day job, and in our workshop we have a very simple system: every machine has a board with the jobs that need to be done, sorted in the order they should be worked on.

I basically wanted exactly that for my game development.



Instead of having things like *"I still need to improve that model"* or *"this texture needs another pass"* floating around in my head, I wanted to create a job, give it a priority and forget about it until it's time to work on it.

Then AI agents entered the picture and the idea became even more useful.



An agent can look at the available jobs, take the highest priority one, work on it and submit the result for review. If I don't like it, I send it back for improvement. The agent never decides what actually goes into my game — I do.

Over the last few days that simple job board grew into **PhlloriLab**.



It now handles jobs for 3D, 2D, sound and code, has previews, project workspaces, Codex/Claude Code support, MCP workflows for creative tools and handoff to Unreal, Unity and Godot.

But the basic idea is still just that workshop board.





**There are jobs. They have priorities. Someone works on them. I review the result.**

I'm now at the point where I actually want to stop developing the tool and start using it for my games. :P

Since it already exists, I thought there was no reason to keep it to myself.

So I've released the Windows version completely free on itch.io:

[https://phllori.itch.io/phllorilab-jobboard](https://phllori.itch.io/phllorilab-jobboard)

I'm going to keep using and improving it as part of my own development workflow.





Maybe some of you will find it useful too. :)

comments.author: NullzeroJP
comments.body:
Very cool or you to share.

Can you tell me how you solved saving work items in your list system ? Are you saving them to a database or anything? Just curious.

replies.author: Phllori
replies.body:
Thanks! I kept it pretty simple. There's no database, everything is stored locally as JSON files.

Each job has its own folder with a `job.json` and its working files. The project itself also has a small `phllorilab_project.json`.

I actually like it this way because you can open and read everything yourself, it's easy to back up or move around, and the agents can work with the same files directly.

Nothing fancy, but it works well for what I need. :)

comments.author: Eirdeth
comments.body: Any chance you’d want to share the GitHub instead of a Windows binary?

replies.author: Phllori
replies.body: I don't really plan to put it on a public GitHub repo, but if you'd like to have a look at the source code or play around with it yourself, I'm happy to share it with you. :)

replies.author: Plenty-Mix9643
replies.body: I would love to have the sourcecode. Can you send me an PM? Thanks for this great project.

replies.author: Phllori
replies.body: Sure! I’m preparing a cleaned-up source package with build instructions and a license, since I don’t want to send the messy development folder as-is. I’ll send you a private link once it’s ready. :)

comments.author: Phllori
comments.body: The source code is now also available at [https://phllori.itch.io/phllorilab-jobboard](https://phllori.itch.io/phllorilab-jobboard)  .. have fun with it.

comments.author: Phllori
comments.body:
PhlloriLab – Update 1.0.28

All changes since release 1.0.3



This update introduces local sound and pixel art generation to PhlloriLab, adds an option for the agent to handle Aseprite editing, and brings improvements to Claude, Cascadeur, and the Unreal handoff.



\- Local sound generation: Codex or Claude formulates the prompt based on the project context and job description. Stable Audio Open generates the sound locally; finished, validated WAV files are automatically moved to the "Review" stage and can be played back directly via the integrated player. Audacity and its associated MCP integration have been removed from PhlloriLab.



\- Pixel art with selectable options: The new "Agent with Aseprite MCP" checkbox determines the workflow. If unchecked, the local image AI (Tiny-SD) generates the image. If checked, the agent creates or edits the pixel art using the configured Aseprite MCP. This selection is saved per job and carried over when duplicating jobs. If the MCP is missing, the agent reports the reason instead of switching to the local AI.



\- Textures via large image models: Texture jobs utilize the executing agent's available large-scale image generation capabilities. The small local image AI remains restricted to pixel art.



\- Visible generation progress: Sound and local pixel art generation display processing steps, percentage completion, and elapsed time. The app monitors the generation process independently, even after the agent has handed off the prompt and ended the turn. Sound and images are calculated sequentially; temporarily locked progress files no longer cause the generation process to abort.



\- AI setup in the settings: Separate download and install buttons for the sound AI and pixel art AI display the installation status. These models are installed separately and are not included in the main setup package. Once set up, local generation runs offline; License confirmation remains required for Stable Audio Open. NVIDIA systems receive CUDA-enabled PyTorch during setup.



\- Intentional editor window opening: GIMP and Aseprite are launched via their respective editor buttons. Automated image processing takes place without an editor window; existing source files remain protected.



\- User-controlled roadmap: Entries can be added, edited, checked off, deleted, and reordered. For Codex and Claude, the roadmap serves as read-only context; only the assigned job is executed.



\- Codex model selection: The model can be selected directly within the job. The selection is saved and passed to the launched job; the model actually resolved is displayed.



\- Claude integration fixed: Current Claude desktop installations are now detected even with an additional subdirectory. Aseprite-MCP now launches correctly regardless of the job folder. Claude outputs are read as UTF-8 to ensure umlauts display correctly.



\- Cascadeur for characters and animation: These jobs prioritize the use of Cascadeur. PhlloriLab prepares the local MCP/script server and verifies its availability before the agent starts. Blender remains a documented fallback option if Cascadeur is unavailable after an attempted launch.



\- 3D transfer via Blender roundtrip: "In Blender" prepares the roundtrip using the job name, export folder, blueprint name, Unreal project, and content destination. The last selected import mode is retained. This workflow replaces the separate PhlloriLab 3D importer.



\- Sound to Unreal: Approved WAV files can be imported as SoundWaves in the background via "To Unreal." Existing destination assets are not overwritten. Standalone game instances and active "Play In Editor" sessions are rejected for the import. Failed imports are assigned a "completed" job status and display the specific error.



\- Refined local AI integration: The previous general local AI/LM Studio integration has been removed. Local models are now specifically dedicated to sound and pixel art.



Windows setup versions are available.
